script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for August 18. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Climbing stairs leaves you winded.  Climbing mountains leaves you exhausted.  Going up fights gravity—it costs energy.

Going up means working against Earth's gravity. Every foot of elevation requires lifting your weight that distance. It's never free. This is why elevation costs energy—it's physics, not weakness. Height provides perspective—you see more from above.  It provides safety—threats are below.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Going up is hard—that's why high ground is valuable.  The effort creates the advantage.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Climb Assessment - Where Are You Going Up?.

Here's your activity: Where in your life are you 'climbing'—working toward elevation? Is the pace sustainable? What's the view from where you are now? Sometimes pausing to appreciate progress gives energy for the next stage of the climb. This helps you evaluate climbing efforts and sustainability.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about going up can be applied to climb assessment - where are you going up?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
